The most important gap is the fix loop's classify step (verified / best-effort / reverted) and the five-fix self-check, which the flow omits even though its stop rule counts reverts. Setup rules on tooling, evidence storage and real credentials are also not shown.

code.overview: /qa is carried out entirely by the agent following skills/qa.md: no script starts the app, runs probes, assigns severities, counts reverts or writes the report. The only code is scripts/test-qa-skill.sh, which greps the skill text so its rules cannot be dropped, the wrapper check in scripts/resolver-phases.ts that keeps the /qa command pointing at that text, and the pre-commit hook that each fix commit passes through.

refs.anchor: export function phaseWrapperIntegrity(rows: ResolverRow[], { fail, SKILLS_DIR, CURSOR_RULES, ANTIGRAVITY_SKILLS, ANTIGRAVITY_WORKFLOWS, rel }: PhaseCtx): void {
refs.title: Wrapper integrity: each harness wrapper must point at the skill file
refs.explain: For every registered skill it builds the expected path skills/<name>.md. It then opens each harness wrapper that exists (Claude, Cursor, Antigravity skill and workflow) and fails the check if the wrapper does not contain a reference to that path. It runs from scripts/check-resolvable.ts, in the pre-commit hook and in npm test.
refs.why: This is the only code on the way into /qa: it guarantees the command loads skills/qa.md and not a stale copy. Everything after that entry is the agent following the text.

refs.anchor: has "$S" 'diff-aware|git diff'                  "scopes probes to the diff by default"
refs.title: qa skill test: surfaces, clean tree, diff scope
refs.explain: Three case-sensitive greps require the bold surface names browser, API and CLI in skills/qa.md. Two more require the text 'git status --porcelain' and either 'diff-aware' or 'git diff'.
refs.why: Pins the setup rules in the text: the surface list, the clean-tree check, and scoping probes to the diff. Nothing here runs git status or picks surfaces; the agent does that.

refs.title: has / has_cs / finish: the assertions the skill tests are built from
refs.explain: ok and fail print a line and bump a counter. has runs a case-insensitive extended-regex grep over a file and records pass or fail; has_cs is the case-sensitive form. finish prints the totals and returns non-zero if anything failed.
refs.why: Shows what the skill acceptance tests can and cannot prove: they only check that a phrase is present in the skill text. They never run the flow or watch what an agent does.

refs.anchor: has "$S" 'regression test'                      "regression test before each fix"
refs.title: qa skill test: fix-loop rules
refs.explain: Four greps over skills/qa.md require the phrases 'regression test', '/investigate', 're-run' or 're-verify', and 'two reverts'.
refs.why: Keeps the fix loop's rules in the text: a regression test per fix, diagnosis through /investigate, re-running the probe, and the stop rule. The revert count and the 30-fix cap are tracked by the agent, not by code.

refs.anchor: echo "pre-commit: ESLint configured but not installed — skipping (install deps, e.g. npm ci)" >&2
refs.title: pre-commit hook: lint and mechanical check on staged files
refs.explain: staged lists the staged files that match a pattern. If an ESLint config exists and ESLint is installed, the staged JS/TS files are linted. Then, if the mechanical check script exists, it runs with --staged. A non-zero exit from either step aborts the commit (set -eu).
refs.why: Each QA fix is its own commit (fix(qa): QA-NNN), so with hooks enabled every fix is linted and mechanically checked before it lands. The hook does not check the commit message, the regression test, or that the probe was re-run.

refs.anchor: has "$S" 'blocked'                              "unreachable surface is reported blocked, not passed"
refs.title: qa skill test: blocked status, summary line, feature-chain wiring
refs.explain: Greps skills/qa.md for 'blocked' and for 'QA found'. Then greps skills/feature-chain.md for '/qa' and for 'QA'.
refs.why: Pins that an unreachable surface is reported as blocked, that the report ends with the one-line summary, and that the feature chain calls /qa and repeats that line. The report itself is written by the agent.

promptOnly.what: The agent runs git status --porcelain, picks surfaces from git diff main...HEAD --stat, starts the app the way the repo documents, polls for readiness, and uses only seeded or synthetic data.

The agent drives each entry point with good and bad input using the repo's own tools, saves evidence outside the repo, logs each issue as QA-NNN with severity and repro steps, and marks unreachable surfaces blocked.

The agent sorts issues by severity, applies the quick, standard or exhaustive tier, defers the rest, and stops here in --report-only mode; the test only checks that the three tier names appear in the skill text.
The agent follows /investigate for each in-tier issue, writes the failing regression test, fixes, re-runs the probe, commits, and counts reverts and fixes itself to decide when to stop.
The agent re-runs every probe near a fix plus the happy path on each surface and puts any regression first in the report.
The agent fills in the report table and summary line, writing docs/<feature-slug>/qa-report.md inside the feature chain or printing it in chat when standalone.
